summary: Practise ICSR validation, causality assessment and safety reporting workflows. Explore the pharmacovigilance course and review its practical curriculum.
lede: Pharmacovigilance operations training covers how medicine-safety professionals handle individual safety reports and evaluate potential signals. Regulatory staff, pharmaceutical safety teams, and health-programme professionals practise validating cases, assessing seriousness and causality, selecting MedDRA terms, and planning follow-up. Exercises also cover ICH E2B(R3) reporting workflows, signal prioritization, and quality checks, while AI-assisted triage is introduced as operational awareness rather than implementation training.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for medicine safety case processing, signal review, or pharmacovigilance reporting across regulatory, manufacturer, and health-programme settings.
prerequisites: Relevant work in medicines regulation, pharmaceutical safety, clinical research, or health-programme operations is useful. No programming is required. Bring a basic understanding of medicine safety reporting in your work context; the course introduces the named pharmacovigilance methods and standards used in its exercises.
